# References: Branches, Tags, and HEAD

After this page you can say what a ref is, where it lives, and how HEAD relates to a branch.

## A ref is a name for a hash

A **ref** (reference) is a name that points at a commit (or, for annotated tags, at a tag object). Git stores them as files under `.git/refs/` and, when there are many, in `.git/packed-refs`.

| Ref | Typical path | Meaning |
|-----|--------------|---------|
| Branch | `.git/refs/heads/main` | Movable name for a line of work |
| Tag | `.git/refs/tags/v1.0` | Name meant to stay put |
| Remote-tracking | `.git/refs/remotes/origin/main` | Last-seen tip of a branch on a remote |
| HEAD | `.git/HEAD` | Where you are |

```bash
git rev-parse main
git rev-parse HEAD
cat .git/HEAD
# ref: refs/heads/main
```

`git rev-parse` turns a name into a hash. Use it when a diagram and the disk disagree in your head.

## Branches move, tags mostly do not

```bash
git branch                  # local branches
git branch feature          # new name at current HEAD
git switch feature          # HEAD now points at feature
git switch -c hotfix        # create and switch
```

`git switch` is the modern command for changing branches (`git checkout` still works; this book uses `switch` for branches and `restore` for files).

A tag is a bookmark:

```bash
git tag v0.1                # lightweight: a name at HEAD
git tag -a v0.1 -m "first"  # annotated: a tag object
```

Moving a published tag surprises people who already fetched it. Moving a branch is normal.

## HEAD is usually a pointer to a pointer

```text
.git/HEAD          →  ref: refs/heads/main
.git/refs/heads/main →  a1b2c3d4….
```

Commit while on `main`: Git writes a new commit whose parent is `a1b2c3d4…`, then overwrites `refs/heads/main` with the new hash. HEAD did not change its text; the branch it names did.

**Detached HEAD:** `.git/HEAD` contains a raw hash instead of `ref: refs/heads/…`. You get there with `git switch --detach`, or by checking out a tag. To keep work from a detached HEAD:

```bash
git switch -c keep-this
```

That creates a branch at the current commit and attaches HEAD to it.

## Remote-tracking names

After you add a remote named `origin` and fetch (chapter 11):

```text
refs/remotes/origin/main
```

That is *your* last photograph of `main` on that remote. It updates on fetch. You do not commit onto it. Your local `main` is a separate name you push.

## Plumbing vs porcelain

`git branch`, `git switch`, `git tag` are **porcelain** (human commands). `git update-ref` and `git symbolic-ref` are **plumbing** (the same operations, no sugar). This book stays on porcelain until internals (chapter 16). Knowing refs are files is enough to understand why creating a branch is cheap: Git writes a 41-byte file.
